question: Doxycycline is the drug of choice for all rickettsial infections, including scrub typhus, and should be started empirically in a febrile patient with an eschar without waiting for confirmatory serology.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Doxycycline is the first-line empirical treatment for all rickettsial infections. The eschar of scrub typhus (in concealed skin folds — groins, axillae, behind ears) is pathognomonic and clinically confirms the diagnosis; waiting for serology wastes critical treatment time.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Doxycycline (100 mg twice daily for 7–14 days) is the drug of choice for all rickettsial diseases. Confirmatory serology (Weil-Felix, IgM IFA) is retrospective and should never delay treatment — untreated scrub typhus has mortality up to 30% and responds dramatically within 48 hours of doxycycline.
